questions.scenario: Two VPCs need a simple private connection and there is no expected third VPC or central inspection requirement. Which option has the least routing machinery?

options.text: VPC peering with nonoverlapping CIDRs and routes on both sides.
A full Transit Gateway hub.
A public internet gateway on both VPCs.
An S3 gateway endpoint.

questions.explanation: VPC peering can fit a small point-to-point topology. Transit Gateway becomes valuable as connectivity and policy centralization grow. Learn more in [Transit Gateway architecture](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/how-transit-gateways-work.html).

questions.scenario: Twenty workload VPCs need shared services and centralized inspection, with separate production and development routing domains. Which design fits?

options.text: A full mesh of 190 peering connections.
Transit Gateway attachments with separate TGW route-table associations and propagations.
One shared subnet for all accounts.
Public IPs plus security groups.

questions.explanation: Transit Gateway provides a hub and multiple route tables for segmented connectivity at scale. Learn more in [Transit Gateway route tables](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/tgw-route-tables.html).

questions.scenario: The production attachment is associated with a production TGW route table, but development routes are propagated into that same table. What is the risk?

options.text: Association prevents all propagation.
TGW ignores CIDR routes.
Propagation can unintentionally make development destinations reachable from production.
The VPC local route deletes propagated routes.

questions.explanation: Association chooses the table used to route traffic from an attachment, while propagation adds attachment routes to tables. Both must match segmentation intent. Learn more in [Transit Gateway route tables](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/tgw-route-tables.html).

questions.scenario: App VPC can send packets to a database VPC through TGW, but replies never return. Security groups are correct. What route condition is most likely missing?

options.text: A public Route 53 record.
An S3 prefix-list route.
A second internet gateway.
A return route from the database-side VPC and TGW table toward the app CIDR.

questions.explanation: End-to-end reachability requires a valid forward and return route across VPC and TGW route tables. Learn more in [Transit Gateway architecture](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/how-transit-gateways-work.html).

questions.scenario: A shared Transit Gateway will connect production, development, inspection, and shared-services VPCs. Which controls reduce the multi-VPC routing blast radius?

options.text: Separate TGW route tables for trust domains.
Propagate every attachment into every table by default.
Explicit association and propagation review.
Use public IP addresses to avoid reviewing route propagation.
Nonoverlapping, governed CIDR allocation.

questions.explanation: Segmentation, deliberate propagation, and governed address allocation keep the hub from becoming unrestricted transitive connectivity. Learn more in [Transit Gateway route tables](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/tgw-route-tables.html).
